title: Olist E-Commerce Analytics
summary: An end-to-end Brazilian e-commerce analytics project using Python, SQL, and Power BI to analyze sales, customer behavior, delivery performance, and marketplace growth.
problem: Understand how customers, orders, products, sellers, and delivery performance affect marketplace revenue and customer satisfaction.
findings: Analyzed approximately 96K orders and 93K customers.
Total product revenue reached approximately 13.22M, excluding freight.
The repeat customer rate was approximately 3%.
Average review scores declined from 4.3 to 1.7 for deliveries delayed by seven or more days.
São Paulo contributed approximately 39% of revenue.
The top 10 product categories generated approximately 62% of revenue.
Freight costs represented up to 28% of product price in remote states.
notes: Includes Python notebooks, SQL scripts, data profiling reports, and the original Power BI report.

title: CRM Sales Pipeline Analysis
summary: A sales performance analysis using SQL and Power BI to evaluate revenue against targets, identify performance gaps, and compare sales representatives and managers.
problem: Identify why the sales team is missing its targets and highlight the managers and sales representatives contributing to the performance gap.
findings: Total sales reached 10M, while the team finished 4M below target (-27.5%).
Every manager finished below target.
Dustin Brinkmann recorded the widest performance gap at -55%.
Only 4 of the top 10 salespeople achieved their targets.
Darcel Schlecht recorded the highest positive target gap at +40%.
Percentage-based target gaps provide fairer comparisons when sales targets differ.
notes: Includes SQL preparation scripts, a Power BI dashboard, and project documentation.

title: Ames House Price Prediction & Analytics
summary: An end-to-end housing price prediction project using the Ames Housing dataset, covering data preprocessing, exploratory analysis, feature engineering, and machine learning.
problem: Investigate housing features and evaluate machine learning models for predicting residential property prices.
dataset: Ames Housing dataset – House Prices: Advanced Regression Techniques.
findings: Linear Regression achieved an RMSE of 52,659 and an R-squared score of 0.638.
Random Forest achieved an RMSE of 29,331 and an R-squared score of 0.888.
XGBoost achieved an RMSE of 26,294 and an R-squared score of 0.910.
XGBoost achieved the best performance among the three evaluated models.
notes: Uses the Ames Housing dataset and is separate from the King County housing project. The repository README describes a Power BI dashboard, but its exact downloadable file path has not yet been verified.
